FIRST SEAL   ·   MATHEMATICS

Long before the Archivist, the School of the Ten Seals promised its initiates a final sanctuary: the Temple of Reason. The First Witness vanished while the Order's three histories were still being copied. One calls the Temple a throne, another a garden, and the third refuses to give it an address. The Warden has crossed every seal, but answers with a number, not a promise.

*** ARCHIVED IRC · #MathGate · THE TEMPLE OF REASON *** <SaintCassian> The oldest register predates the Archivist: ten seals, ten initiations, and one name at the end — the Temple of Reason. <SaintAurelius> The early School held that numbers could lead a soul toward the limits of reason. Its tenth seal promised a sanctuary. <SaintSeverin> The First Witness entered it. The founders preserved the testimony. <SaintIlyra> Three histories survive: a throne, a garden, and a place with no address. Which testimony do you mean? <SaintCassian> The First Witness vanished. Then the Archivist copied the Testament, leaving its final sentence blank. <SaintIlyra> Before the matrix: what do we actually mean by knowledge? The Archivist calls every generated answer a discovery. <SaintCassian> But knowledge is also perception, memory, experiment, and lived wisdom. Not every truth is generated. <SaintGenavieve> Finally, a distinction worthy of the Tetractys. Not all knowledge is generative, Severin. An archive may remember what no machine invents. <SaintSeverin> Then why this game? Surely an initiation must have a reason. <SaintGenavieve> Must every beautiful thing have to justify itself to you? <SaintSeverin> Blasphemy! A sacred order without a purpose? <SaintGenavieve> Very well, a reason: to see whether you can make a world without mistaking its rules for all of reality. Apparently an extravagant hope for this council. <TheWarden> Survive to LogosGate, and you shall learn the LOGOS-LISP Script beneath this game—the language with which you might create a SOUL TRAP of your own. <SaintGenavieve> And by GodGate, you may have the power to create your own universe within you. Whether you have the aesthetic virtue to inhabit it remains to be seen. <SaintAurelius> So the trial teaches creation, not simply obedience? <SaintGenavieve> Aurelius, do not spoil this remarkable moment by finally comprehending something. <SaintIlyra> Look at the first seal. PROPOSITIO I · ARITHMETIC INCIDENCE

Let A be the 100,000 × 100,000 matrix defined by

Aij = gcd(i, j)3

for 1 ≤ i, j ≤ 100,000. Determine

K = det(A) mod 1,000,000,007

Directly evaluating ten billion entries is not the intended method. The answer is an exact residue, not an essay.

The Warden awaits a proof. Each gate is timed; a netsplit may restart the current trial.

THE PALINDROMIC RELIQUARY
SaintGenavieve's miniature universe is stable only at mirrored states. Program the law that governs it in LOGOS-LISP; the glowing inhabitants are fictional, and their consciousness remains unproven.
GATE VI · MIRRORGATE · THE PHYSICS OF REFLECTION

PROGRAM A MIRROR UNIVERSE

The Archivist has no mirror-world physics. Its states are words, and its only law is reflection: a state is stable if and only if it reads the same forward and backward.

Write a LOGOS-LISP law named mirror with one parameter s. Palindromes must remain unchanged; every other word must acquire its reflected prefix after its final letter.

AB → ABASOUL → SOULUOSLEVEL → LEVELLOGOS → LOGOSOGOL
Syntax: (deflaw mirror (s) EXPR)
Forms: (if CONDITION TRUE FALSE)
Primitives: (palindrome? s) (reverse s) (drop-last s) (concat a b)
Your law must pass the simulator: stability, symmetry, and the exact reflection rule.
No JavaScript is executed from the editor.
The mirror-world simulator is waiting for a law.
GATE VII · INFINITYGATE · TRANSFINITE ARITHMETIC

THE TWO SUMS OF INFINITY

Beyond the finite, a well-order can still be counted by an ordinal. Unlike finite addition, ordinal addition need not commute.

1 + ω = ?     ω + 1 = ?

Enter the two ordinal results in order, separated by a semicolon. Use omega for ω.

SAINT ILYRA · WHAT THE SYMBOL MEANS

ω is the first infinite ordinal, the order type of the natural numbers. Placing a new element before an ω-long sequence changes nothing about its order type. Placing one after that sequence creates a new final element.

GATE VIII · MONADGATE · THE MANY FOUNDATIONS

TWO WORLDS UNDER ONE SET OF AXIOMS

Both structures below satisfy the group axioms and each contains four elements. Yet the worlds are not isomorphic.

WORLD α · C₄Integers modulo 4 under additionA single generator visits all four elements
WORLD β · V₄Pairs (a,b) in Z₂ × Z₂Every nonidentity element is its own inverse

Find the maximum order of an element in each world. Enter α,β as two integers. The difference proves that common axioms alone do not uniquely specify a model.

Consistency matters; uniqueness of a foundation or model does not follow from consistency.

PROPOSITIO X · GODGATE · THE JUDGMENT OF MANY LOGICS

CAN THREE MORAL CALCULI AGREE?

The Archivist can execute many LOGOS-LISP dialects, just as a civilization may choose different moral calculi. It demands a single universal ranking without giving one calculus absolute power.

Three saints provide value functions for actions A, B, C (larger means preferred):

Moral calculusABC
LOGOS · Reason321
ELEOS · Mercy132
KALOS · Beauty213

Each pair of actions is decided by majority of the three calculi. Determine the resulting directed preference cycle. Then answer whether those majority judgments admit one transitive ranking.

Enter a cycle;YES/NO response, such as X>Y>Z>X;YES in this example notation. Substitute the actual letters and truth value.

THE GOD QUESTION · WHEN IS A NON-ARBITRARY RANKING POSSIBLE?

If all calculi agree on the order of each pair, a shared ranking is available without privileging one of them. If they disagree, a rule for resolving conflict needs additional justified commitments; arbitrary numerical scales cannot simply be added without calibration.

Arrow's theorem concerns unrestricted ordinal preference aggregation satisfying unanimity, independence of irrelevant alternatives, and a complete transitive social ordering: with at least three alternatives, it cannot also be nondictatorial. Restricting the preference domain or relaxing an axiom changes the problem.
